name: Addicted
body:
You are dependent on some substance or habit that gives you both a disadvantage and an advantage.

Prerequisite(s): 3 ranks in the addiction’s relevant skill (see below).

Benefit(s): When you take this feat, select an addiction from the list below. You can gain this feat multiple times, each time selecting a different addiction.

Every time you indulge in your vice, you take a number of minor penalties and gain a benefit associated with your addiction, as indicated below. Indulging always requires 1 hour minimum.

If you have at least 12 Hit Dice, you also gain the first boon granted by your addiction. If you have at least 16 Hit Dice, you gain the addiction’s second boon as well. If you have 20 Hit Dice or more, you also gain the addiction’s third boon.

Addictions

Authors’ Note: The Addicted feat is presented as a narrative character option that provides more bonuses but also some drawbacks to represent certain addicted characters in media of all kinds. We do not intend to present this as promoting unsafe drug use in any way. If you or anyone you know is suffering from an addiction, Call the SAMHSA hotline 1-800-662-HELP (4357) if in the U.S. If outside the US, please consult your country/county/territorial helpline.

Unless a specific duration or number of uses per day is listed, a boon‘s effects are constant.

If you ever fail to indulge in your vice in a day you lose all access to resistances and boons granted by this feat until the next time, and may suffer the effects of withdrawal associated with your addiction. If you are healed of damage, conditions, or penalties caused in the course of indulging in your vice, you similarly lose all boons granted by this feat, but don’t suffer from withdrawal.

If your addiction is cured by magic, you lose access to this feat until you have developed a new addiction (this requires 30 consecutive days indulging in the same vice or a different one). Alternatively, you can decide to stay cured and immediately exchange the Addiction feat with another. You can also detoxify yourself voluntarily by spending 30 consecutive days without indulging in your vice, suffering all the time from the effects of withdrawal. At the end of this period, you can lose the Addiction feat and replace it with another.

Addiction: Behaviors

Maybe you have to count every tile you put your foot on. Maybe you are a compulsive collector of cockroaches. You could wax your moustaches every day, or you could hate sharing your food. Be it for a superstition, a psychic disturbance, or simply an obsession, your behavior leaves a distinct impression of eccentricity in everyone you meet.

Relevant Skill: Sense Motive.

Indulge: Pass time practicing your behavior or diffusely talking about it to someone who’s not interested. You suffer a -4 penalty on Persuade and Stealth skill checks and cannot benefit from magic effects that would allow you to go unnoticed or undetected. Your maniacal attention to details grants you a +4 bonus on all Perception and Sense Motive skill checks.

Boon 1: You have an unnerving talent for asking the right questions. You can cast confess as a spell-like ability twice per day.
Boon 2: You have a highly specialized knowledge in a field related to your compulsive behavior. You can always take 20 on one category of Knowledge skill checks. If you use the optional rules to research facts and lore, you can complete a research in 1 hour rather than 1 day and can expend inspiration points instead of influence points to this purpose. If you use the library research rules, you gain a bonus on research checks equal to ½ your character level.
Boon 3: You can read the environment around you to find tiny clues and piece together the events transpired there. This works as retrocognition, except that the reconstructed events can happen up to 1 day in the past for every 2 character levels you possess.

Withdrawal: When you can’t indulge in your maniacal behavior, you are overwhelmed by anxiety. You develop a lesser madness that can’t be cured until you can return to your behavior or are cured from the addiction.

Addiction: Entertainment

The fine arts for some are an interest, and even a passion. For you, they are an obsession. You must experience the highs crescendos and low dramatic tragedies. Experiencing great artistic endeavors inspires you and distills your focus for the coming day.

Relevant Skill: Perform or Artistry.

Indulge: You must experience a performance of some kind, be it an art display at a museum, an ally using their Perform skill or a concert or play. Roll a d20, with a result of 1-10 the performance was satisfactory but nothing special and you gain no bonus. With a result of 11-15 the performance was great and you gain a +2 morale bonus on Will saves for 24 hours. With a result of 16+ the bonus to will saves increases to +4. If an ally performs for you with the Perform skill, you gain a +1 bonus on this roll for every 5 of their check results. You may also increase the bonuses of this roll if no ally is involved by spending 5 gp per +1 bonus, the more expensive performances are more likely to inspire you. You may attempt to perform for yourself but you do not gain any bonuses from money or the check result as you gain more from hearing and learning other methods.

Boon 1: You understand the bolstering power of music and can relate the salient details to an ally. Once per day, you may cast heroism as a spell-like ability.
Boon 2: You can perform for your allies and bolster their morale. Three times per day, you can grant your allies a morale bonus to attack rolls, Will saves and skill checks equal to 1/4 your HD for 1 minute. Boon 3: Your ability to inspire your allies through your performances reaches immense heights. You may cast heroic invocation once per day as a spell-like ability.

Withdrawal: If you have not experienced a performance of some kind, you have difficulty focusing. To be able to cast spells or use point pools like inspiration or panache for any class ability you must make a Concentration check of 10 + the spell level or ½ their class level for pool point usage. If they fail, they cannot get the inspiration to perform the task, though they do not lose the point of Inspiration.

Addiction: Food

Be it to calm a constant anxiety, to fill an internal void, or to clear your mind, nothing gives you the same pleasure as engorging yourself with food and sweet drinks.

Relevant Skill: Craft (alchemy).

Indulge: Feast carelessly, alone or with your friends, until you are completely satiated. You have weight issues and are always encumbered. When a critical hit or sneak attack is scored on you, there is a 20% chance that the critical hit or sneak attack is negated and damage is instead rolled normally.

Boon 1: There’s nothing like food to make someone open their heart. You gain a morale bonus on all Bluff and Persuade checks equal to your character level.
Boon 2: You gain DR 10 against slashing and piercing damage.
Boon 3: You are immune to poisons. You also can always find poison in food or beverages as with detect poison.

Withdrawal: If you can’t eat your fill, you feel weak, suffering a -2 penalty on all Strength- and Constitution?based die rolls.

Addiction: Gaming

Dice, cards, chess, whatever. You cannot stop. You cannot stand to lose. You could sell all your goods to stake them on the next game. But you swear you can tell who will be the winner next time…

Relevant Skill: Bluff.

Indulge: Play your favorite game with at least 1 other player. Roll 1d20. With a result of 1-10, you lose 1/10 of all your gold. With a result of 11-20, you win an equal amount. You also gain a +4 bonus on all Appraise checks for 24 hours.

Boon 1: Winning is just a matter of calculating the odds. You may cast cleromancy once per day as a spell-like ability.
Boon 2: Whoever makes the first move has an advantage. You gain Improved Initiative as a bonus feat. If you already have Improved Initiative, you instead add +10 ft. to your land speed.
Boon 3: Knowing the rules allows you to find loopholes. You may cast time stop once per day as a spell-like ability.

Withdrawal: If you can’t play, you can’t sleep or rest properly. You are fatigued and require double the usual time to regain your spells.

Addiction: Substances

You are dependent on alcoholic drinks or other drugs. These blur your judgment but can give you surprising insights and resistance to external control.

Relevant Skill: Heal.

Indulge: Consume a massive dose of your chosen beverage or drug. You gain all the bonuses and damages listed for that substance. You also gain a +4 bonus against mind-affecting and language-dependent effects for 24 hours.

Boon 1: Once per day, you can go on a rampage of intoxicated fury, functioning as the blood rage spell at a caster level equal to your character level.
Boon 2: Your mind can work at an accelerated speed while you are under the effect of your chosen substance. Three times per day, you can roll twice any ability check or skill check involving a mental ability and take the better result.
Boon 3: Your altered state of mind has opened the doors of perception for you, and leaves you in a psychedelic state that almost transcends space and time. You can cast foresight on yourself only as a spell-like ability once per day.

Withdrawal: You suffer the effects of a moderate addiction to your chosen substance. This addiction can’t be cured by any amount of consecutive saves.
